name: Runs and trails
blurb: Flat loops, wooded ravines, and 27 paved miles that cross the whole city.

places.name: Burke-Gilman Trail
places.note: 27 paved miles from Ballard through the U District and out to Bothell. The spine of running and cycling here.
places.address: Burke-Gilman Trail, Fremont, Seattle, King County, Washington, 98013, United States

places.name: Discovery Park
places.note: 534 acres above the Sound. The 2.8-mile Loop Trail is the one, and the bluff opens onto the Olympics.
places.address: Discovery Park, 3801, Magnolia, Seattle, King County, Washington, 98199, United States

places.name: Green Lake Park
places.note: The default loop. 2.8 miles, flat, lit at night, and busy enough that running alone never feels like it.
places.address: Green Lake Park, 7201, Green Lake, Seattle, King County, Washington, 98115, United States

places.name: Elliott Bay Trail
places.note: Flat waterfront miles from Myrtle Edwards north. Container cranes on one side, ferries on the other.
places.address: Portside Trail, Yesler Terrace, Seattle, King County, Washington, 98134, United States

places.name: Washington Park Arboretum
places.note: 230 acres of trees with soft paths through them. Go in April for the azaleas.
places.address: Washington Park Arboretum, 2300, Madison Park, Seattle, King County, Washington, 98112, United States

places.name: Interlaken Park
places.note: A wooded ravine between Capitol Hill and Montlake. Steep, quiet, and shaded the whole way.
places.address: Interlaken Park, Capitol Hill, Seattle, King County, Washington, United States

places.name: Myrtle Edwards Park
places.note: The downtown-adjacent stretch of waterfront path. Where people run on a lunch break.
places.address: Myrtle Edwards Park, Belltown, Seattle, King County, Washington, United States

places.name: Seward Park
places.note: Loop the peninsula, then cut into the old-growth trails in the middle when you want dirt.
places.address: Seward Park, Seattle, King County, Washington, 98118, United States
